q: Medical reimbursement to railway employees is admissible ___.

options.A: As per rules for treatment taken under prescribed conditions

q: Settlement of medical claims requires ___.

options.B: Verification of bills and sanction by the competent authority

q: Powers to sanction medical reimbursement are delegated ___.

options.D: In the hierarchy, with finance concurrence where required

q: Which statement is true about medical claims?

options.C: Claims must be supported by genuine bills and prescriptions

q: An employee submits a medical reimbursement claim for emergency treatment at a private hospital. The claim should be ___.

options.A: Examined and settled as per rules by the competent authority

q: Which is NOT correct about reimbursement?

options.C: Any amount can be claimed without bills

q: Reimbursement for treatment at recognised hospitals is generally ___.

options.D: More straightforward than at non-recognised hospitals

q: The role of finance in medical claim settlement is to ___.

options.B: Ensure correctness and admissibility of the claim

q: Time limits for preferring medical claims exist to ___.
Medical reimbursement claims are sanctioned by ___.

options.B: The competent medical or finance authority as per delegation

q: Inadmissible items in a medical bill are ___.
Which statement is true about medical reimbursement rules?

options.A: Rules differ arbitrarily from person to person
options.D: Reimbursement rules apply uniformly to eligible beneficiaries

q: An employee treated in a railway hospital generally ___.

options.A: Gets cashless treatment as per entitlement
options.D: Must go to a private hospital

q: For treatment taken at a non-recognised hospital in an emergency, reimbursement ___.

options.C: May be considered as per rules with proper justification

q: Which of the following is NOT a valid supporting document for a medical claim?

options.A: Cash memo or bill from the hospital

q: Delegation of reimbursement sanction powers helps in ___.
Higher-value medical claims are sanctioned by ___.
Which statement is true about finance concurrence in claim settlement?

options.B: It applies only to officers' claims
options.D: It is presumed required unless specifically exempted

q: Scrutiny of medical claims protects against ___.
An employee aggrieved by rejection of a claim may ___.

options.C: Represent to the higher authority as per procedure

q: Which of the following is NOT correct about medical reimbursement?

options.C: Reimbursement is a matter of right without rules

q: Medical advance for treatment may be sanctioned ___.

options.D: As per rules by the competent authority

q: Adjustment of medical advance is done ___.

options.B: Against the final claim as per rules
options.D: By writing it off in every case

q: The competent authority for reimbursement at the divisional level functions ___.

options.A: Within the delegated powers of the medical administration

q: Which statement best summarises reimbursement powers?

options.D: Sanction by the competent authority, within delegation, with finance concurrence where required

q: Central Hospital Administrators in JAG or Senior Grade exercise the powers of a ___.
Equating Central Hospital Administrators (JAG/SG) with Branch Officers means that they ___.
A Branch Officer in the delegation hierarchy is ___.

options.A: Below Senior Scale and JAG officers

q: Which statement is true about Central Hospital Administrators?

options.C: Central Hospital Administrators (JAG/SG) exercise Branch Officer powers

q: A Central Hospital Administrator (JAG) sanctions an item of expenditure. His sanction is valid if ___.

options.A: It is within the Branch Officer powers delegated under the MSOP
options.B: He is in JAG so any amount is fine
options.C: No finance concurrence ever applies to him

q: The purpose of equating JAG/SG Hospital Administrators to Branch Officers is ___.

options.B: To give them General Manager powers
options.D: To define their delegated powers clearly

q: In the powers hierarchy, a Branch Officer ranks below ___.

options.B: Senior Scale, JAG, DRM, PHOD and GM

q: Which of the following is NOT correct about Hospital Administrators' powers?

options.A: Branch Officers are the lowest in the given hierarchy
options.B: JAG officers generally outrank Branch Officers except for this specific equation
options.C: This equation gives them PHOD powers
options.D: Hospital Administrators (JAG/SG) have Branch Officer powers

q: A Senior Grade officer posted as Central Hospital Administrator exercises ___.
The specific mention of Central Hospital Administrators in the MSOP indicates ___.

options.A: Clarity on their delegated powers for hospital administration
options.D: That the MSOP does not apply to them

q: Branch Officer powers are exercised ___.

options.D: Within the limits delegated under the MSOP

q: Which level is immediately above Branch Officer in the stated hierarchy?
If a matter exceeds Branch Officer powers, the Central Hospital Administrator should ___.

options.A: Refer it to the higher authority

q: The JAG/SG designation of the Hospital Administrator refers to ___.

options.D: The grade or scale of the officer

q: Which statement is true about delegation to Hospital Administrators?
A Central Hospital Administrator exercising Branch Officer powers must still obtain finance concurrence ___.

options.B: Wherever required under the presumption rule

q: Which is NOT correct about the Branch Officer level?

options.A: Hospital Administrators (JAG/SG) are equated to it
options.B: Powers at this level are limited
options.D: It is a defined level in the delegation hierarchy

q: Day-to-day administrative decisions of the Central Hospital are taken by ___.

options.A: The Railway Board on a daily basis
options.D: The Hospital Administrator within delegated powers

q: The equation of JAG/SG Hospital Administrators with Branch Officers is an example of ___.
Which authority is higher than a Central Hospital Administrator exercising Branch Officer powers?

options.B: Senior Scale and above in the hierarchy

q: In case of doubt about his powers, the Hospital Administrator should be guided by ___.

options.A: The MSOP delegation and the higher authority

q: Which statement is true about the scope of Hospital Administrators' delegated powers?

options.A: All JAG officers automatically get PHOD powers
options.B: Grades do not matter in delegation
options.D: Only the specified Hospital Administrators (JAG/SG) are equated to Branch Officers for this purpose

q: The delegation to Central Hospital Administrators covers ___.

options.C: Hospital administration matters within Branch Officer powers

q: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of delegated powers?

options.C: They flow from higher to lower authority
options.D: They require finance concurrence where applicable

q: A Hospital Administrator's sanction beyond Branch Officer powers would be ___.

options.D: Irregular and subject to regularisation by the competent authority

q: Railway health units or dispensaries primarily provide ___.
Health units on railways function under the ___.
Powers relating to the running of health units include ___.
A health unit is generally headed by ___.
Which statement is true about health units?

options.A: They function without the medical department
options.B: They are the first point of medical contact for beneficiaries

q: Medicines for health units are supplied ___.
Which is NOT correct about health units?

options.C: They are part of the medical department
options.D: They refer serious cases to hospitals

q: Serious cases presenting at health units are ___.
The medical officer in charge of a health unit exercises ___.
Hygiene and sanitation at health units is ___.
Health units maintain records of ___.
Which statement is true about the administration of health units?

options.B: Health units are run by contractors
options.C: Health units function within the delegated powers framework
options.D: Health units are outside the MSOP

q: Immunisation and preventive care at health units ___.

options.A: Are part of their public health role

q: A new health unit is opened ___.

options.D: With sanction of the competent authority as per rules

q: Which of the following is NOT a function of a health unit?
Emergency cases at health units are handled ___.

options.B: With first aid and referral as needed

q: The running of health units requires finance concurrence ___.

options.A: Wherever required under the presumption rule

q: Health units in a division are supervised by ___.

options.D: Senior medical officers of the division

q: Health units contribute to ___.

options.A: Preventive healthcare of railway staff and families

q: Which statement is true about dispensary stocks?

options.C: They are accounted for as per procedure

q: Periodical inspection of health units ensures ___.
Which of the following statements about health units is NOT correct?

options.D: They can purchase anything without sanction

q: Medical officers at health units may issue ___.
Coordination between health units and hospitals ensures ___.
The overall responsibility for health units in a zone rests with ___.

options.A: The CMD as PHOD of the medical department

q: Visiting specialists may be engaged by railway hospitals ___.

options.C: On contract as per delegated powers

q: Engagement of specialists on contract is resorted to when ___.

options.C: The speciality is not available in-house

q: The terms of engagement of visiting consultants include ___.

options.D: Honorarium or remuneration, duties and tenure as per sanction

q: Which statement is true about specialist engagement?

options.B: It requires sanction of the competent authority

q: A CMS wants to engage a visiting cardiologist on contract. He should ___.

options.A: Process the engagement within delegated powers, with finance concurrence where required

q: Which is NOT correct about engaging specialists?
Honorarium to visiting specialists is paid ___.
Contract engagement of specialists helps railway hospitals ___.

options.A: Provide specialised care without permanent posts

q: Engagement of visiting consultants is sanctioned by ___.

options.D: The competent authority as per the delegation hierarchy

q: The tenure of a contractual specialist is ___.

options.B: As specified in the terms of engagement

q: Which statement is true about engaging specialists on contract?

options.C: Specialists can be engaged for specific specialities as needed
options.D: Specialists must be engaged for all departments

q: The performance of visiting specialists should be ___.
Finance concurrence for specialist engagement is required ___.
Which of the following is NOT a valid reason to engage a visiting specialist?
Engagement of specialists on contract is different from regular appointment because ___.

options.A: It is for a defined tenure and terms

q: A visiting consultant's duties are ___.

options.C: Defined in the terms of engagement

q: Which statement is true about renewal of specialist contracts?

options.B: Renewal needs fresh sanction as per rules

q: The competent medical authority proposing specialist engagement must ___.

options.A: Justify the need and follow delegation and finance rules
options.C: Skip finance concurrence in every case

q: Which of the following is NOT correct about specialist engagement?

options.B: Any officer can create permanent specialist posts

q: Visiting specialists supplement ___.
The honorarium rates for visiting consultants are ___.

options.C: As sanctioned by the competent authority

q: Which statement is true about the nature of contractual engagement?

options.A: Contractual engagement does not create a permanent post
options.B: Every contract creates a permanent post
options.C: Contracts are appointments to gazetted posts

q: Emergency engagement of a specialist may be done ___.

options.A: Without any procedure in every case

q: Documentation of specialist engagement is needed for ___.
Which statement best summarises specialist engagement powers?

options.B: Need-based engagement on contract with competent sanction and finance concurrence where required
